boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 15:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.15.1), immediately followed by the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.15.2) at 15:2, which puts the riddle about the useless vine-wood in the standard oracle-onset frame. Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:24 opens with no fresh formula device, וַתִּבְנִי לָ֖ךְ גֶּ֑ב וַתַּעֲשִׂי לָ֥ךְ רָמָ֖ה בְּכָל רְחֽוֹב (oshb:Ezek.16.24), continuing the word-event unit by default and cataloguing the addressee's promiscuity against Egypt, Philistia, Assyria and Chaldea in turn (16:26-29). Close side: the row is taken through 16:34, whose final clause וַתְּהִ֥י לְהֶֽפֶךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.34) ('and you became the opposite') closes the reversal-of-a-prostitute's-wages figure just before the summons לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.16.35) ('therefore, prostitute, hear') opens at 16:35. The utterance formula recurs at 16:30, מָ֤ה אֲמֻלָה֙ לִבָּתֵ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.16.30), but sits mid-verse there, with the clause on the deeds of a brazen prostitute still to follow, so it is weighed and not treated as a row-final refrain. The paragraph layer records a pe on 16:35, one verse AFTER this row's own close at 16:34, not on 16:34 itself; that is disclosed rather than smoothed over, because it means the mark corroborates a seam one verse later than the addressee-shift onset this row's boundary is actually argued from. MT 16:25 (oshb:Ezek.16.25) carries a single Ketiv/Qere note, reading the ketiv תזנתך in the running text. MT 16:31 (oshb:Ezek.16.31) also carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span, one of five verses in this chapter carrying a doubled note: the running text reads the ketivs עשיתי and הייתי, against the Qere readings עָשִׂ֖ית and הָיִ֥ית (oshb:Ezek.16.31, Qere for both); neither Qere is used to argue this boundary.

MT 16:51 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.51) the ketivs אחותך and עשיתי, with the Qere layer giving אֲחוֹתַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.51, Qere) and עָשִֽׂית (oshb:Ezek.16.51, Qere). An editorial note also falls at 16:54 inside this span, disclosed as a single-witness vowel-reading divergence, not a text-critical claim about the row's content.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the pe recorded at MT 18:32 (single witness) closes the preceding unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam; MT 19:1 itself opens with the distinct qinah-command onset וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.1) ('and you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel') -- not a word-event formula and not a son-of-man address, but the genre-naming command proper to a lament. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own colophon, MT 19:14, the whole verse וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֨יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.19.14), whose last clause names its own genre a second time ('this is a lamentation, and it is used as a lamentation'), matched by a pe recorded on this same verse. A pe also falls mid-chapter, on 19:9, at the close of the lion-cubs figure (אֲרָי֖וֹת, oshb:Ezek.19.2) -- לְמַ֗עַן לֹא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.9) ('so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel') -- immediately before the second figure opens at 19:10, אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.19.10) ('your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water'). That internal mark is disclosed and weighed, not adopted as a row seam: the colophon at 19:14 names the whole composition, both figures together, a single lamentation, so the span is kept as one row rather than split at its own internal parashah break.
